lead: Anaheim plumbing deals with hard water, slab homes from the 1950s and 1960s, and earthquake rules. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Anaheim.
risk: slab leaks, aging galvanized and cast-iron pipes and hard water scale
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes and hard water
why: Anaheim boomed in the 1950s and 1960s, and many homes from that time still have galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. The Colony, near downtown, has even older homes.
Most homes sit on slabs, so supply leaks under the floor are common. California requires water heaters to be strapped for earthquakes.
water: Anaheim Public Utilities blends local groundwater with water imported through the Metropolitan Water District. The water is hard. The city utility also supplies electricity.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Scope cast-iron drains in older homes.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Anaheim, the Colony, Anaheim Hills, West Anaheim, the Platinum Triangle and every other Anaheim neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Anaheim Planning and Building Department, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Why do 1950s Anaheim homes have plumbing problems?
faq.a: Many were built with galvanized steel supply pipes and cast-iron drains. After 60-plus years, the steel rusts inside and the cast iron cracks. Repiping and drain lining are common fixes.
